summary.headline: Exide Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 20.3% YoY to INR5,026 crore and EBITDA margin reached 12.1%, with 6 GWh lithium cell plant commissioned.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR5,026 crore, up 20.3% YoY, taking H1 revenue to INR10,331 crore (up 18.9%), the first half above INR10,000 crore. EBITDA rose 53.6% YoY to INR606 crore, with margin at 12.1% versus 9.4% on a weak base, while H1 margin was 12.2%. Management said the 6 GWh lithium-ion cell plant in Bengaluru was commissioned on 23 September 2026, with LFP revenue starting in October and NMC revenue expected from the major OEMs around February. Management guided to staying within a 12-12.5% EBITDA margin corridor for the next two quarters, and said it is avoiding buying market share.

segments.name: Automotive OEM
segments.commentary: Grew over 25% YoY for the fourth consecutive quarter; management cites about 60% share in automotive OEM and wins on MG Hector Tomahawk and Tata Aeris launches.

segments.name: Replacement (two- and four-wheeler)
segments.commentary: Delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, helped by a growing vehicle parc and distribution reach.

segments.name: Home inverters and solar
segments.commentary: Home inverters grew 20% YoY; solar grew over 40% YoY, supported by seasonal demand and PM Surya Ghar Yojana.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew over 20% YoY for the second consecutive quarter, on a low base; a long-term cooperation agreement with ExCom Energy Solutions GmbH (Germany) was signed in September for the European Economic Area.

segments.name: Industrial infrastructure (ex-telecom)
segments.commentary: Grew high single digits, driven by industrial UPS and traction motive power; government tenders (railways, power) stayed muted.

segments.name: Lithium-ion (Exide Energy Solutions)
segments.commentary: 6 GWh Bengaluru plant commissioned 23 September 2026; two 1.5 GWh NMC lines commissioned; LFP (102 Ah) revenue started October 2026; BESS cell line (line four, 300+ Ah) ready but awaiting PLI clarity.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin to stay within a 12%-12.5% corridor at current lead and rupee levels for the next two quarters, with some quarters at the lower end and some at the higher end.
Passenger vehicle and two-wheeler demand growth expected to moderate to maybe low double digits in Q3 on a percentage basis; aftermarket to normalise in H2 at H1 levels.
Major lithium OEM NMC revenue expected from around February 2027 (beginning of Q4); small customers from the next month; all in this fiscal year.
Lithium-ion business targeted to become cash neutral in two to three years; phase two capex decision expected around 80% utilisation of the 6 GWh plant.
Core lead-acid capex about INR400-500 crore per year, in line with depreciation; ACC phase-two capex to be presented to the board, with a possible update next quarter.
Price increases of about 9-10% on four-wheeler and about 5% on two-wheeler since January, with further calibrated increases in October.
capex_capacity: 6 GWh lithium-ion cell plant in Bengaluru commissioned 23 September 2026; first phase capex largely complete, with working capital and ramp-up funding to follow.
Land bought for 12 GWh with utilities for 12 GWh already in place on the same campus; phase-two lead time expected to be shorter than phase one.
Two 1.5 GWh NMC lines commissioned; first line to be filled before the second is used.
Lead-acid debottlenecking across multiple factories and additional capacity discussions with automotive OEMs for conventional IC engine vehicles.
Management said the rupee weakness could raise capex per kWh in phase two unless equipment prices fall.
Depreciation to rise in H2 as the new plant capitalised on 23 September 2026 is fully reflected.
demand_pricing: Vahan data: two-wheeler registrations up 1.3 million (32%) and passenger vehicles up 0.3 million (27%) YoY in Q2; last year's Q2 base was weak ahead of GST 2.0.
Electric two-wheelers were about 11.6% of two-wheeler retail in September; E2W registrations near 2 lakh per month, about 7.5-8 GWh of current market.
Cell cost gap of about 5-10% versus imported Chinese cells on a landed basis, offset partly by strategic benefits such as local sourcing.
Lithium pricing is indexed, with the reference being the landed price from China.
Management said the company will not buy market share during a growth phase; share gains are coming from weak categories and geographies.
Input costs remained elevated due to West Asia tensions and a weaker rupee; full benefit of lower lead and antimony prices was not realised.

qa_highlights.question: Is lithium revenue being recognised, and when will NMC revenue for two-wheelers start?
qa_highlights.answer: LFP revenue started in October; small NMC customers can start next month in small quantities, and major OEMs are expected from early Q4 or February, all within this fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: Can lead-acid margins hold around 12% with high-single-digit growth in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin will stay within the 12-12.5% corridor for the next two quarters; percentage OEM growth will moderate, but absolute volumes stay at higher levels and aftermarket normalises to H1 levels.

qa_highlights.question: What are the phase-two lithium capex trigger and expected margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase two decision is expected at about 80% utilisation; no lithium margin guidance is given yet because dollar-per-kWh pricing is uncertain. The goal is cash neutrality in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost gap between Exide cells and imports?
qa_highlights.answer: A 5-10% landed-cost gap versus imported Chinese cells remains, offset by strategic benefits such as a second local source for OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS cell plan given the PLI scheme?
qa_highlights.answer: Line four (300+ Ah) is ready for BESS cells, but the company will wait for PLI clarity before going to full production.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the depreciation line lower despite the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The new plant was capitalised only for seven days in Q2 (23 September); core-business depreciation fell as older assets completed their lives. H2 depreciation is expected to be higher.

risks_watch: Rupee depreciation raising input costs and phase-two capex per kWh.
Lithium NMC validation timelines and OEM approvals; customer names are under NDA and no order book is disclosed.
China export controls on raw materials for lithium cells could extend lead times and raise inventory and working capital needs; a three-month inventory hold is planned.
Working capital and operating losses for the lithium business until it becomes cash neutral in two to three years.
Hyundai-Kia co-investment for a dedicated line is still under discussion and no timing is given; joint statement to follow at a milestone.
Government BESS localisation and PLI clarity may delay BESS cell production.
Mark-to-market losses on HDFC Life investment (about INR600 crore in H1).
summary.management_tone: Confident on core lead-acid demand, pricing pass-through and the lithium commissioning, while cautious about H2 OEM growth moderating. Evasive on Hyundai-Kia timing, lithium margins, phase-two capex and the BESS roadmap, citing NDAs, material disclosure and the need for board approval.
key_quotes: Overall, the demand held up well across our addressable markets during the quarter two.
We will not buy market share just for the sake of it.
We still have a 5% -10% cost gap with imported Chinese on landed basis, based on the form factor and chemistry.
Should be. Yes, you are right. It depends upon our operational excellence also.

growth.why: Q2 standalone revenue up 20.3% YoY with H1 up 18.9%, backed by strong auto OEM (25%+), replacement and export demand plus price increases and the 6 GWh Bengaluru lithium plant commissioned in September; management guides EBITDA margin in a 12-12.5% corridor for two quarters but gives no explicit revenue growth number, and NMC revenue timing (around Feb 2027) and phase-two capex remain undecided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin within a 12-12.5% corridor for the next two quarters versus 12.1% in Q2 and 9.4% a year ago, so margins hold near current levels rather than expand much, with cost tailwinds from lower lead and antimony prices not yet fully realised.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 6 GWh Bengaluru lithium plant was commissioned 23 Sep 2026 with two 1.5 GWh NMC lines commissioned, LFP revenue started October 2026 and major-OEM NMC revenue is expected around February 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Automotive OEM grew over 25% YoY for four straight quarters and replacement grew double digits for four quarters, but management expects PV and 2W growth to moderate to low double digits in Q3 and aftermarket to normalise to H1 levels.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Phase-two lithium capex decision is tied to about 80% utilisation of the 6 GWh plant, which is only just commissioned, and ACC phase-two capex goes to the board with a possible update next quarter.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is holding a 12-12.5% margin corridor and says it is avoiding buying market share, and it gives no explicit revenue growth number to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flags H2 OEM growth moderating, a weaker rupee and elevated West Asia-linked input costs, and China export controls on lithium-cell raw materials that could extend lead times and working capital.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: NMC cells for major lithium OEMs are expected around February 2027 and small customers from the next month, while the BESS cell line (300+ Ah) is ready but waiting on PLI clarity.

rows.label: Hyundai-Kia co-investment for dedicated line
rows.why: Discussed as under discussion with no timing; a joint statement is to follow at a milestone, so it is not yet firm.

rows.label: Further calibrated price increases
rows.why: Prices already rose about 9-10% on four-wheelers and about 5% on two-wheelers since January, with further calibrated increases flagged for October.

rows.label: Lithium business cash neutral
rows.why: Management targets cash neutrality in two to three years, but the business still carries operating losses and working capital needs, with a three-month inventory hold planned.

tone.note: Management was confident on lead-acid demand, price pass-through and the lithium commissioning, but cautious on H2 OEM growth moderating; analysts pressed on Hyundai-Kia timing, lithium margins, phase-two capex and the BESS roadmap, which management largely deferred citing NDAs and board approval.
